name: Shebna
description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Rabshakeh, the ambassador of the Assyrian army, spoke for the king to convince Judah to yield. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah asked him to speak in the Syrian language, not in the Jews' language in the ears of the people on the wall. History note from class: the Assyrians and the Syrians were two distinct peoples whose languages intermingled; the Syrians are the children of Aram, Shemites, so Aramaic is Syrian, and through the migrations Aramaic slowly began to replace the paleo Hebrew we spoke.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall will not understand, but he refuses.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and tell him the words of Rabshakeh.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: Eliakim and Shebna and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language, which they understand, and not in the Jews' language in the ears of the people on the wall. They do not want the people to hear the threats.
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and tell him the words of Rabshakeh. They bring the blasphemy before the king in mourning.
He sends Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet. He calls it a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy.
